While I agree it appears that way, the things that it gives you makes those permissions needed. Frankly, these are innocuous, but appear much worse because of the way Google handles permissions. For example - phone status and identity? This is needed to be able to initiate a call. Edit, send, receive, etc with texts? They use that to confirm your identity. You can also text someone not on messenger. Camera access? To take a picture to send in messenger. Mic access? To record audio you can send to a friend on messenger. Read your contacts? Well if you want to sync contacts, it needs to read them.

In other words, yes they look outrageous for a messaging app, but in reality the 'scariness' of those permissions has more to do with how Google shows them than what the app is doing.
